additional_info.subject: ID0441968-DC/Si-D/FR-[MP / R5 170001863]"24VDC_Fuse_FC12_to_FC17" Error CRM:02698000379
additional_info.body:
Hello Théo, good afternoon.
I checked the logs and it seems that around your 12pm there was a failure in the income fuse. Afterwards, someone opened the door and clicked on the Shutdown charger instead of rebooting and that is why when you got there, it was needed to press FC12.
We have 2 options here:
Either there is a component that is short circuited somewhere and we need to figure out which one by going on-site the next time we are there and confirm it.
Or there is something wrong upstream that is causing the fuse to trip.
I will try to find more conclusive information and bring it back to you, but for example, the problem happened again today morning and there was a reboot.
Please request to leave the charger in error and check which fuse is tripped when it's present otherwise we won't be able to troubleshoot it properly.
Thank you very much for your support.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0441968-DC/Si-D/FR-[MP / R5 170001863]"24VDC_Fuse_FC12_to_FC17" Error CRM:02698000379
additional_info.body:
Hello Théo, good morning.
I checked the problem from yesterday and it seems that the mainbreaker tripped to one of the devices on these Fuses FC12 to FC17.
Unfortunately, right after, someone clicked on the "Shutdown" button on the screen instead of reboot and that is why, when you reached the site, it was completely off and it only needed to be pressed FC12.
Remotely, I cannot check which the fuse was tripped since the Error Flag is the same for all. The idea here is that when this error reoccurs, we need to check on-site which Fuse is tripped to identify the root cause.
Please request to leave the charger in error in case this happens so that we can provide you a solution.
Let me know your thoughts and questions.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
